title: Expense Agent: Finance Controlling (2026 release wave 1)

chapters.title: Expense report creation and billable information
Posting the expense report and ledger entries

features.name: Expense Agent
features.description: An agent that processes expenses submitted in the web app and automatically flows data through the system, including dimension tracking and ledger entry creation.
caveats: Employee dimensions cannot be specified manually; only accountant can add or move dimensions after submission

features.name: Default dimensions on employee records
features.description: Dimensions attached to an employee (such as department and sales person) are automatically pulled through to expenses submitted by that employee.

features.name: Billable information on expenses
features.description: Employees can assign expenses to customers, specify a G/L account, and link them to project and project task numbers. These sources combine to create a new set of dimensions.

features.name: Posted expense report ledger entries
features.description: When an expense report is posted, it creates multiple entries: the expense report itself, project ledger entries, and employee ledger entries to track money owed to the employee.

features.name: Pay employee function
features.description: A function on the employee card that allows users to view all outstanding employee expenses and create a payment in the payment journal.

features.name: Employee account type in payment journal
features.description: A new account type called 'employee' in the payment journal for paying out employee expenses. Previously only vendor account type was available.

features.name: Project billable cost tracking for expenses
features.description: Expenses assigned to a project appear in the project's billable cost section and are categorized by expense type (e.g., other travel expenses).

quotes.why_it_matters: Establishes the scope: this video covers the Expense Agent feature and its end-to-end data flow in Business Central.

quotes.text: And we're going to see a bit about how data is flowing through our system automatically. So one thing that Lena cannot do herself
quotes.why_it_matters: Clarifies a key design decision: employees cannot manually specify dimensions; the system uses default dimensions from the employee record to automate tracking.

quotes.text: And then the accountant can choose to add or move um dimensions. So in this case the accountant has added a business group.
quotes.why_it_matters: Shows the workflow: after an employee submits an expense, the accountant retains the ability to adjust dimensions before posting.

quotes.text: And there she can assign the uh expense to a customer. She can even specify which account in our system it should go to,
quotes.why_it_matters: Describes the billable information feature allowing expenses to be assigned to customers and specific G/L accounts.

quotes.text: And there's also a ledger entry for the employee, because now we owe Lena this money.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains the business logic: posting an expense report creates an employee ledger entry representing a payable to the employee.

quotes.text: And as you can see that we now have an account type that's called employee. Previously, it would have been only a vendor, but
quotes.why_it_matters: Marks a feature addition: the payment journal now supports 'employee' as an account type, not just vendor.
